title: Preparation and Characterization of Graphene-Based 3D Biohybrid Hydrogel Bioink for Peripheral Neuroengineering
protocol: Take Wharton's jelly mesenchymal stem cells out of a −80 °C freezer.
Culture WJ-MSCs in DMEM-F12 medium containing 10% fetal calf serum (FBS), 1% Pen-Strep, and 1% L-glutamine in a sterile laminar flow at room temperature.
Count 1 x 10^6 cells on a Thoma cell counting slide.
Add the freezing solution dropwise to the counted cells.
Transfer the slide quickly to a liquid nitrogen container for cryopreservation.
Pour out the medium when cultured cells are 80% confluent in the flask.
Wash with 5 mL of PBS.
Add 5 mL of 0.25% trypsin and 2.21 mM EDTA-4Na.
Incubate in an incubator at 37 °C for 5 min.
Add 10 mL of DMEM-F12 medium with 10% FBS to the cells removed from the incubator.
Suspend it well, collect the medium, and transfer the medium to a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at a rotational speed of 101 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and re-seed the cells in new flasks with fresh nutrient medium containing 10% FBS.
Mix WJ-MSCs with bioinks to form a 3D control group.
Add 0.1% graphene to the bioinks containing WJ-MSCs to create a 3D Graphene-Bioink Biohybrid Group.
Form WJ-MSCs into spheroids and place them on the bioinks for a 3D Control of Spheroid Form group.
Mix WJ-MSCs with 0.1% graphene in spheroid form on the bioinks to create a 3D Graphene-Bioink Biohybrid Group of Spheroid Form.
Prepare 3D bioink drops for SEM and FTIR characterization analysis.
Create 3D graphene drops by adding graphene to bioinks, then prepare them for SEM and FTIR characterization analysis.
Weigh 100 µg of graphene nanoparticles.
Add 10 mL of DMEMF-12 medium with 10% FBS to the weighed graphene.
Label this solution as stock solution.
Sterilize in an autoclave at 121 °C under 1.5 atm pressure for 20 min.
Store the sterile graphene mixture in the refrigerator at 4 °C until use.
Prepare mixtures of medium with different concentrations of graphene (1%, 0.1%, 0.01%, 0.001%, and 0.0001%).
Determine non-toxic doses through these initial dilutions.
Take 1 mL from a 1% stock solution of graphene.
Transfer the taken solution into a new tube.
Add 9 mL of DMEMF-12 medium with 10% FBS to each tube.
Shake and vortex the solutions to ensure equal distribution.
Use only 10 mL of DMEMF-12 medium with 10% FBS as control.
Seed WJ-MSCs in 6-well plates with 2 mL of fresh medium containing 10% FBS at a density of 5 x 10^5 cells per well.
Incubate the plates for 1 day at 37 °C.
Divide the plates into groups of equal and repeated wells.
Do five repetitions for each concentration.
Discard the medium from the wells after incubation.
Replace the medium with graphene concentrations in fresh medium at 2 mL per well.
Use only the medium without graphene for the control group.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C for 24 h.
Discard media containing graphene after 24 h of incubation.
Wash each well with PBS to remove excess graphene nanoparticles.
Add fresh DMEMF-12 medium with 10% FBS at 2 mL per well.
Use MTT protocol to determine the IC50 value indicating 50% cell viability.
Weigh out 5 mg/mL of MTT salt and dissolve in PBS.
Sterilize the MTT solution using a 0.45 µm filter.
Wrap the sterilized MTT solution in aluminum foil and store at 4 °C.
Add 10 μL of MTT to all the wells of the plate.
Incubate the plate for 4 h at 37 °C.
Observe the formation of formazan crystals at 10x magnification under the microscope after incubation.
Add 100 µL of DMSO to each well and mix by pipetting.
Keep the plate in the dark at room temperature for 30 min.
Insert the plate into the ELISA plate reader.
Set a wavelength of 570 nm from the program for absorbance measurement and read the plate.
Perform statistical analysis on the obtained results using one-way ANOVA with Tukey's test in a statistical analysis program.
Turn on the computer first.
Turn on the time-lapse imaging incubator and set it to 37 °C.
Place the MTT plate in the time-lapse incubator slot.
Open the Stitch program on the computer.
Specify the wells to be read in the system.
Bring the reader to the first well and locate and focus the area at 10x magnification in white light.
Start the program.
Weigh 4.5 mg of alginate and transfer to a centrifuge tube.
Transfer 1.5 mg of gelatin to the same centrifuge tube.
Add DMEMF-12 medium containing 10% FBS to the mixture to a total volume of 50 mL.
Repeat weighing 4.5 mg of alginate and transferring it to a new centrifuge tube.
Transfer 1.5 mg of gelatin to the new centrifuge tube.
Take 50 µL of prepared 0.1% graphene from step 2.1.3 and add to the new tube.
Add DMEMF-12 with 10% FBS to a total volume of 50 mL in the new tube.
Mix the bioinks first by pipetting.
Vortex the mixed bioinks.
Sterilize the mixtures in an autoclave at 121 °C under 1.5 atm pressure for 20 min.
Alternatively, sterilize the mixtures by microwaving until boiling point.
Centrifuge the autoclaved mixtures at 280 x g for 2 min at room temperature to remove bubbles.
Keep the bioinks at 37 °C until cells are prepared.
Wash the cells when there is 80% confluence with approximately 5 mL of PBS.
Add 5 mL of 0.25% trypsin and 2.21 mM EDTA 4Na to the cells.
Incubate for 5 min at 37 °C.
Remove the incubated cells from the incubator and add 10 mL of DMEM-F12 medium with 10% FBS.
Suspend the mixture well, collect the medium, and transfer it to a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the collected medium at 101 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Leave approximately 250 µL of medium with the pellet.
Redissolve the pellet in 1 mL of fresh medium.
To 48 µL of medium, add 2 µL of cell suspension and 50 µL of trypan blue (0.4 g trypan blue/100 mL) in a conical tube (1.5 mL).
Pipette the mixture well.
Add approximately 10 mL of the prepared stained cell suspension to a Thoma cell counting chamber.
Calculate the average number of cells falling into the squares on both sides of the light microscope.
Calculate the vitality percentage (%) = (counted viable cells/total cells counted) x 100.
Count the cells for group 1 so that there are approximately 1 x 10^7 cells in 0.5 mL of medium.
Add 4.5 mL of bioink to bring the total volume to 5 mL.
Transfer this mixture to cartridges in the sterile cabinet with the help of syringes.
Install the cartridges in the corresponding extruder section of the bioprinter.
Take 5 mL from each of the bioink groups and transfer them to sterile cartridges using an injector.
Set the X/Y/Z resolution per microstep to 1.25 µm, the extrusion width to 400 µm, and the extrusion height to 200 µm.
Use the bioprinter with two coaxial printheads and pneumatic-driven extrusion technology for printing.
Create 3D models using open-source, web-based CAD programs.
Design simple 3D models with one of the platforms (e.g., infill).
Export the model in .stl format as a 5 mm x 20 mm x 20 mm square.
Wipe the bioprinter device with 70% ethanol before operation.
Sterilize the bioprinter by UV sterilization.
Transfer bioink groups to cartridges using an injector.
Install cartridges in the corresponding extruder section of the bioprinter.
Set the average pressure of the 3D printer to 7.5 psi.
Set the cartridge and bed temperature to 37 °C.
Set the speed to 60%.
Put the system in the home position during the writing phase.
Select the extruder and set parameters.
Start the printing process.
Take the printed sample after bioprinting.
Place the printed sample under a laminar flow cabinet.
Spray the bioinks with 0.1 N CaCl2 solution after printing.
Add 1 mL of 0.1 N CaCl2 solution to the printed patterns using a pipette at room temperature.
Wait for about 10-20 seconds.
Wash the printed patterns twice with PBS containing Ca2+ and Mg2+.
Add 2 mL of DMEMF-12 medium supplemented with 10% FBS on top of each cell-containing bioink group.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C in an atmosphere of 5% CO2.
Add 2 mL of suspension medium containing 1 x 10^6 cells to each group for spheroid formation.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Observe the spheroid formation under an inverted microscope after 24 hours of incubation.
Photograph all batches of bioink after 24 hours of incubation.
Add 2 mL of neurogenic differentiation medium per well (except for the control group) and refresh every 2 days.
Follow the process for 7 days to observe neural differentiation.
Prepare the FT/IR microscope and align the optics of the instrument.
Calibrate the FT/IR device.
Place a 1-2 mm thick hydrogel drop on the sample part using forceps.
Focus on the sample and raise it until close contact is made.
Collect the sample spectrum by starting the process from the system.
Drop the hydrogel into 6-well plates containing 1 mL of CaCl2 crosslinker using a pipette tip droplet method.
Wash the plates 2x with approximately 1 mL of PBS to free the solution of salts.
Put the drops into a falcon tube containing 5 mL of 5% paraformaldehyde using forceps.
Make thin sections from the drop bioinks with the help of a scalpel.
Stick the samples on the sticky side of the metal plate.
Insert the coated samples into the coating device where gold palladium covers the sample.
Put the sample in the electron microscope (SEM).
Open the SEM connected microscope program.
Perform scaling and take images of different parts of the sample using 5 µm, 10 µm, and 200 µm scales.
Take a total of 40 images for the 3D-B and 3D-G groups.
Add commercially available 1 x 10^7 GFP-labeled MSCs into 5 mL of bioink.
Bioprint as per step 3.2.11.
Add 1 mL of crosslinker, hold for 20-30 seconds, then wash twice with PBS.
Turn on the time-lapse monitor and open the program on the computer.
Set approximately 16 hours in Time-Lapse mode and set the temperature to 37 °C.
Press the Start button.
Focus the microscope at 10x magnification every 2 hours.
Visualize spheroids created by following the same steps.
Collect the spheroids without interrupting sphere forms.
Reseed the collected spheroids into new plates for restaining with an easier method.
Pipette approximately 500 μl of prepared 0.1% gelatin into 48-well plates.
Leave the gelatinous plates in the incubator for 10 min.
Collect the spheroids by pipetting and distribute them from the incubator into the wells of the 48-well plate.
Add fresh medium to the distributed spheroids.
Incubate the distributed spheroids for 12-24 h.
Collect spheroids in a single tube and distribute the total volume evenly among wells.
Wash cells with PBS for 2D samples, removing medium slowly.
Fix cells in 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 hours.
Wash samples with PBS three times.
Block samples with about 10 mL of 2% BSA and 0.1% TritonX for 30 minutes.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with selected primer antibodies diluted to a 1:100 ratio in antibody diluent reagent solution.
Wash samples three times with PBS.
Incubate with anti-mouse IgG-FTIC-rabbit and anti-mouse IgG-SC2781-goat secondary antibodies, each diluted to 1:200 at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Perform all operations in the dark.
Wash secondary antibody samples three times with PBS.
Drip DAPI solution (1:1) into each sample and wait 15-20 minutes.
Perform immunofluorescence imaging.
